item.title: Occupancy Driven Phase Transitions in Gapped Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems characterized by an energy gap between the ground state and excited states support a growing number of thermal excitations upon raising the temperature. Provided these excitations interact with each other, their number affects the size of the energy gap akin to a harmonic oscillator where the oscillation frequency is damping dependent. Here we show that once a critical number of excitations is reached, the excitation population becomes thermodynamically unstable and the system transitions between two states. This transition is marked by a divergence in the specific heat, which does not have to be accompanied by an order parameter, nor by the full closure of the gap. We illustrate the thermodynamics using a simple two level system and superfluid $^4$He as examples, and we argue that the hidden order transition in URu$_2$Si$_2$ is an example of such an occupancy driven transition in the absence of an order parameter.
item.dc:creator: Ian Madden, Alex Kociubinski, Wouter Montfrooij

item.title: Nonlinear Canonical Transformations for Studying Spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2610.30403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ spin models provide demanding benchmarks. Spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. We introduce a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian into a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions, as nonlocal strings can appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.
item.dc:creator: Swarnamoy Ghosh, Thomas M. Henderson, Gustavo E. Scuseria

item.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.31127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.
item.dc:creator: Kamran Behnia

item.title: When can phonon modes be trapped by arbitrarily weak local defects? Rigorous sufficient conditions in a monatomic lattice
item.description: arXiv:2511.03580v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although many studies have shown that localized defects in vibrational lattices can trap localized phonon modes for particular geometries, there has been no general proof of localization for arbitrary localized defects of arbitrarily weak strength. This is distinct from the problem of Anderson localization, where random perturbations are spread across the entire lattice and one aims to prove whether all states become localized. Here, we study the former problem for monatomic 1d and 2d crystals with nearest-neighbor harmonic interactions, corresponding in 2d to square lattices of masses and springs, and prove that arbitrary localized perturbations (such as any finite set of defect masses) that decrease the net mass by any amount must lead to localized states. In contrast, the analogous statement is generally false in 3d. Our proof employs a straightforward variational method, inspired by analogous results for the Schr\"odinger and Maxwell equations, that should be extensible to other discrete systems.
item.dc:creator: Jaden Thomas, Rodrigo Arrieta, Shu-Ching Yang, Arthur J. Parzygnat, Steven G. Johnson

item.title: Critical timescales for chiral state conversion and irreversibility
item.description: arXiv:2604.01918v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-Hermitian systems driven along slow parametric loops undergo non-adiabatic transitions whose outcome depends sensitively on the driving speed, yet no explicit formula has been available for the critical timescale $T_{\mathrm{cr}}$ at which these transitions develop. Using a $2\times 2$ Hamiltonian with circular parameter trajectories, we derive $T_{\mathrm{cr}} = \mathcal{G}\,\ln(1/|\Delta|)$ in closed form for non-encircling loops, phase-shifted loops, offset loops, and loops encircling exceptional points, where $\mathcal{G}$ is a geometry-dependent growth factor and $\Delta$ is the instability seed. This formula sharply separates the regime where the system remains in the averagely dominant eigenstate ($T< T_{\mathrm{cr}}$) from the superadiabatic regime where the instantaneous dominant eigenstate takes over ($T> T_{\mathrm{cr}}$), resolving the apparent tension between the previous literature. We identify two competing seeds: a geometric Stokes multiplier and the finite-precision floor. When the geometric seed vanishes, precision alone governs the transition, yielding $T_{\mathrm{cr}} \propto m\ln\beta$, linear in the number $m$ of digits in base $\beta$ (bits for $\beta=2$). For loops encircling an exceptional point, the Stokes seed only sets an intermediate plateau; the final transition is again seeded by the precision floor, and $T_{\mathrm{cr}}$ remains linear in $m$. This provides a purely forward-evolution manifestation of precision-induced irreversibility [Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207 (2026)], demonstrating that the fundamental limit identified through echo protocols also controls the outcome of slow non-Hermitian dynamics without requiring time reversal. For PT-symmetric energy spectra, $T_{\mathrm{cr}}$ additionally determines the onset of chirality: the dynamics is non-chiral for $T< T_{\mathrm{cr}}$ and chiral for $T> T_{\mathrm{cr}}$.
item.dc:creator: Giorgos Pappas, Diego Bautista Avil\'es, Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Vassos Achilleos
